content.title: 40 Best Hairstyles for Men with Straight Hair
content.text: What Is Straight Hair in Men? Straight hair in men grows without waves or curls, creating a smooth, even pattern from the roots to the ends. This hair type often looks shiny because natural scalp oils spread easily through the hair. Straight hair is easy to manage and works well with many hairstyles, from classic side parts to modern textured cuts. However, it can sometimes look flat or oily. Adding layers, texture, or a little volume helps straight hair look fuller, more balanced, and easier to style for different face shapes and daily routines. Below are the best straight haircuts for men, chosen to add volume, texture, and clean shape for modern everyday styling. Best Straight Haircuts for Men Modern Mullet A Modern Mullet for straight hair keeps the sides tight and clean while the back stays longer for a cool, edgy finish. The top is layered and slightly messy, giving natural lift and smooth movement without looking heavy. This is one of the most effortless Modern Mullet styles for men with straight hair who want clean contrast with a relaxed, layered finish. Blow-dry forward and up using your fingers, then rub in a small amount of Molding Paste to shape the layers and add flexible hold. Burst Fade This Burst Fade for straight hair keeps the sides faded in a smooth arc around the ear, giving a sharp, sporty look while the top stays short and textured. The clean neckline and tight blend make it easy to wear at school or on weekends. Blow-dry the front slightly upward, then use a small amount of Texture Clay to add grip, shape, and light volume. Curtain Bangs Curtain Bangs give you that clean, K-pop-inspired look with a soft middle part that frames your face. The top stays medium length with light layers, while the sides sit neatly around the ears for smooth movement on straight hair. Blow-dry the front forward, then brush it back and split it with your fingers. Finish with Styling Cream for flexible hold and a natural shine. Low Taper Low Taper is a great haircut if you want a neat look without going too short. The top stays longer with natural texture, while the sides and back slowly blend down for a smooth finish. It works really well on straight hair because the shape stays clean and easy to control. Blow-dry the top forward for volume, then use your fingers to shape it. Finish with Styling Cream for light hold and soft movement. Ponytail A clean Ponytail gives you an instant cool, grown-up vibe while keeping your hair out of your face. Leave the front slightly loose for a relaxed look, then pull the rest back at mid-height and tie it tight for smooth shape. This style looks sharp on straight hair because it stays sleek and flows naturally. Blow-dry for extra lift, then tame flyaways with Hydrating Argan Oil for shine. Textured Fringe A Textured Fringe is a go-to cut for a fresh, easy style with natural movement. The top stays choppy and light, while the sides fade down clean for a sharp outline. Push the fringe forward so it rests across the forehead with a soft, messy finish. Blow-dry while finger-shaping, then use Texture Powder to add lift and keep straight hair looking fuller all day. See more choppy and layered looks in Textured Fringe collection. Edgar Haircut The Edgar Haircut is a bold, clean style with a straight, blunt fringe that sits evenly across the forehead. The sides are faded tight and sharp, while the top stays short and smooth for a strong shape. It works best when straight hair is brushed forward for a neat, heavy look. Blow-dry using your fingers, then finish with Molding Paste for control and a soft, natural hold. Crew Cut The Crew Cut is a sporty haircut with a short, even top and a smooth fade that keeps the sides tight and fresh. It looks sharp with straight hair because the texture sits naturally and stays neat all day. Blow-dry forward for a slight lift, then use Texture Powder to add grip and light volume without making it stiff. Perfect for a low-maintenance, confident style. Drop Fade The Drop Fade is a modern haircut where the fade curves lower behind the ear and blends smoothly into the skin. The top stays short with soft texture, which looks extra sharp on straight hair because it sits neat and controlled. Blow-dry forward for a little lift, then shape it with your fingers. Finish with Styling Cream to keep it smooth, natural, and easy to restyle. Bowl Cut The Bowl Cut brings a bold, retro vibe with a smooth, rounded fringe that sits evenly across the forehead and wraps around the head. The sides stay tight and clean, making the shape look sharp and fresh on straight hair. Blow-dry downward for a sleek finish, then lightly finger-shape the ends. Use Pomade for shine and control without making it stiff. French Crop The French Crop keeps hair short and neat with a straight fringe that sits low on the forehead. The top stays lightly textured while the sides and back are trimmed close for a clean shape that works well on straight hair. Blow-dry forward, then finger-shape the fringe. Finish with Styling Cream to add light hold and natural movement without heavy styling or extra shine. Mohawk The Mohawk keeps the sides faded tight while the center strip stays longer and messy for bold height and movement. The top is cut in choppy layers, letting straight hair lift easily without looking stiff. Blow-dry upward, then use your fingers to shape the spikes and back flow. Finish with Texture Clay for strong hold and a matte, textured finish that lasts all day. Shag Haircut The Shag Haircut uses messy layers and a soft fringe to create easy volume and natural movement. The sides stay slightly longer, while the back tapers out for a cool, lived-in shape. It works great on straight hair because the choppy texture adds lift without curls. Blow-dry forward, then finger-shape the ends and finish with Sea Salt Spray for lightweight, beachy texture. Angled Fringe The Angled Fringe gives straight hair a clean, modern vibe with a long fringe cut on a sharp slant across the forehead. The top stays smooth with light layers, while the sides sit neat and slightly tucked for a sleek outline. Blow-dry the fringe forward and sweep it to one side, then use Styling Cream to keep it soft, controlled, and shiny. Side Swept Fringe The Side Swept Fringe is a stylish pick that makes straight hair look fuller without trying too hard. The top stays medium-length with soft layers, while the fringe falls diagonally across the forehead for a relaxed, clean look. Blow-dry forward, then sweep it to the side using your fingers for natural movement. Finish with Texture Powder to add lift and light hold. Skin Fade The Skin Fade gives straight hair a bold, clean finish with sharp contrast and smooth blending. The sides drop down to bare skin around the ears and neckline, while the top stays short and textured for easy control and natural movement. Blow-dry the front slightly upward, then finger-shape it into place. Rub in a small amount of Molding Paste for light hold and a matte look. Pompadour The Pompadour is all about big volume up front with a smooth, lifted shape that looks sharp and confident. The sides stay neatly tapered, while the top is kept longer and brushed back for strong movement, especially on straight hair. Blow-dry upward with a round brush, then finger-shape the height. Finish with Pomade for shine, control, and all-day hold without stiffness. Textured Crop The Textured Crop keeps the top short and choppy with a blunt fringe that sits straight across the forehead for a clean, bold look. The sides fade down tight, making the messy texture on top stand out with extra movement, especially on straight hair. Blow-dry forward, then pinch small pieces with Texture Clay for a light, matte hold that lasts all day. Middle Part The Middle Part gives straight hair a cool shape with long front pieces split evenly down the center. The top stays light and layered, so it falls naturally and frames the face without looking flat. Blow-dry both sides away from the part for soft lift, then smooth the ends with Styling Cream to keep the flow neat, shiny, and easy to restyle. Hard Part The Hard Part is a clean haircut where straight hair is brushed to the side, and a shaved line is cut to show a clear part. The top is kept longer so it has smooth volume, while the sides fade down tight for a fresh look. Blow-dry the top back and over, then use Pomade to keep it in place and add shine all day. Messy Fringe The Messy Fringe keeps straight hair choppy and light, with uneven layers that fall forward and give easy movement. The sides stay slightly shorter, so the fringe stands out without looking heavy. Blow-dry the front down and slightly to the side, then use Texture Powder to lift the roots and create a natural, messy finish. Man Bun A Man Bun looks clean and stylish when straight hair is brushed back smoothly and tied into a tight knot at the back of the head. The sides stay neat while the top keeps natural flow and shine, giving a confident and modern vibe. Blow-dry the hair back for control, then use Styling Cream to tame flyaways and keep the bun sleek all day. Caesar Cut The Caesar Cut is a sharp, low-maintenance style with short sides and a blunt fringe that sits straight across the forehead. It keeps straight hair looking neat while adding light texture on top for natural movement. Blow-dry forward, then work in a small amount of Texture Clay to add grip and hold. Slick Back The Slick Back is a clean, confident haircut with tight faded sides and longer straight hair on top that flows smoothly to the back. It gives a sharp shape while keeping natural volume and shine. Blow-dry straight hair backward using a brush, then smooth it with your fingers for a sleek finish. Apply Pomade for a glossy hold that keeps everything neat and controlled all day. Quiff The Quiff is a bold, high-volume style with short faded sides and longer straight hair on top that lifts up and back for a clean, fresh look. It adds height, movement, and a sporty vibe without looking messy. Blow-dry the top upward while finger-shaping the front into a soft peak. Finish with Texture Clay to lock in texture and keep the volume strong all day. Taper Fade The Taper Fade for straight hair keeps the sides and back short with a smooth fade that blends into the skin near the ears and neckline. The top stays longer, so straight hair falls neatly and shows a clean shape. This haircut looks sharp but still feels natural and easy to style. Ask your barber to keep the fade low and the top layered for movement. Blow-dry the top back, then use Pomade for light hold and shine. Side Part The Side Part is a stylish haircut with straight hair swept neatly to one side for a sharp, fresh look. The top stays longer with smooth volume, while the sides sit shorter and blend in for a polished shape. Blow-dry the front upward and guide it over with your fingers to create natural movement. Finish with Pomade to lock in shine and hold. Faux Hawk The Faux Hawk is a bold, spiky style that keeps the sides tight while the top stands tall with sharp texture. Hair stays longer through the center and fades down clean around the ears, giving a strong shape that works great with straight hair. Blow-dry upward for lift, then pinch small sections with your fingers. Finish with Texture Clay for gritty hold and all-day control. Temple Fade The Temple Fade keeps the sides neat with a sharp fade that starts right at the temples, while the top stays longer for a clean, stylish shape. It adds contrast and makes the haircut look fresh without being too loud, especially on straight hair. This is one of the most versatile Temple Fade cuts for men who want a sharp, clean finish without going too bold. Blow-dry the top forward or up for light volume, then finger-shape and finish with Molding Paste for flexible hold and smooth texture. Comb Over The Comb Over is a clean and stylish haircut with longer hair on top brushed to one side and short sides that look neat. It adds height and gives your face a sharper shape. This style works great on straight hair because it stays in place easily. Blow-dry the top to the side for volume, then shape it with your fingers. Finish with Pomade to keep it smooth and controlled all day. Spiky Hair The Spiky Hair gives a bold, high-energy look with faded sides and a longer top that stands up with sharp texture. This style looks best when straight hair is blow-dried upward to build strong volume and lift. If you love this kind of bold, high-energy texture, see more Spiky Hairstyles that bring the same sharp, defined lift for straight hair. Use your fingers to pinch small sections into defined spikes, then finish with a small amount of Molding Paste for flexible hold and a clean, modern matte finish. Two Block The Two Block is a trendy cut that keeps the sides and back short while leaving the top longer for a smooth, airy shape. It looks sharp on straight hair because the longer top falls naturally and frames the face without effort. Blow-dry forward or slightly parted, then finger-shape for soft movement. Finish with a small amount of Molding Paste to add light hold and keep the layers in place. Ivy League Cut The Ivy League Cut gives a clean, smart look with short tapered sides and a slightly longer top that can be brushed to the side. It works great on straight hair because it lays smooth and keeps a sharp shape all day. Blow-dry the top back and over, then finger-shape for natural movement. Finish with a small amount of Pomade for shine and controlled hold without stiffness. Layered Haircut Layered Haircut keeps hair light and full of movement by cutting the top into soft, choppy levels that flow into longer sides. It looks best on straight hair because the layers sit smooth and show the shape clearly. Blow-dry forward with your fingers to add lift, then finish with a small pinch of Texture Powder to boost volume and give a natural, airy texture. Long Fringe The Long Fringe works great on straight hair, with a longer front that falls over the forehead and shorter sides that keep the shape clean. The top stays layered so it moves easily and doesn’t look flat. Blow-dry forward while using your fingers to guide the fringe. Finish with a small amount of Styling Cream to keep it soft, smooth, and in place all day without making it hard. Mop Top The Mop Top is a cool, relaxed haircut where straight hair falls in soft layers all around the head. The top stays longer, and the sides blend in smoothly with a slightly messy look. It gives a fun, youthful style that feels natural. Blow-dry forward to shape it, then use your fingers to set the layers. Add Texture Powder for light lift and a soft hold. Disconnected Undercut The Disconnected Undercut brings sharp contrast with short, tight sides and a longer top that sits clearly separate for a bold look. The top keeps straight hair smooth and easy to sweep back or over with clean flow. Blow-dry upward for lift, then finger-shape the front for quick control. Finish with Molding Paste to hold the style in place without making it stiff. Short Straight Hair The Short Straight Hair keeps the look clean, sharp, and easy to manage with a low fade that blends smoothly into the skin. The top stays short and even, giving straight hair a neat shape with light texture and natural movement. Blow-dry forward for a soft lift, then finger-shape the front. Use Texture Powder to add grip and keep the style looking fresh all day. Long Straight Hair The Long Straight Hair gives a clean, effortless look with soft layers that fall around the face and sit neatly past the jaw. The middle part keeps it balanced, while the length adds movement and a relaxed, trendy vibe. Blow-dry downward using a brush to keep it smooth, then finger-comb for a natural finish. Apply Styling Cream to control flyaways and add light shine without making it greasy. Bro Flow The Bro Flow is a medium-length haircut where straight hair is grown out and brushed back so it falls naturally around the ears and neck. The top stays longer for soft volume, while the sides are lightly layered so the hair moves and doesn’t look heavy. Blow-dry it backward using your fingers, then spray Sea Salt Spray to add texture and keep the style loose and flowy. How to Choose the Best Hairstyle for Straight Hair Choosing the right straight hairstyle is easier when you follow these steps based on hair type, face shape, and length. By Hair Type Straight hair often looks smooth and flat, so choose hairstyles with layers or texture. Light layering, textured tops, or soft fringes help add movement, reduce flatness, and make straight hair look fuller and more stylish. By Face Shape Face shape matters when choosing straight hairstyles. Round faces look better with height on top, square faces suit side parts, long faces need width, and oval faces work with most clean or textured styles. By Hair Length Hair length changes how straight hair looks and behaves. Short styles need texture to avoid stiffness, medium length adds movement, and longer straight hair works best with layers to prevent it from looking flat or heavy. How to Ask Your Barber for a Straight Haircut Use these simple steps to explain your straight haircut clearly, so your barber understands your style, length, and overall look. Explain the Style You Want Tell your barber how you want your straight hair to look. Say if you prefer a clean, textured, or natural style. Mention if you style your hair daily or want a low-maintenance haircut that stays neat. Show a Reference Photo Bring one or two photos of straight haircuts you like. Photos help your barber understand the exact shape, top length, and finish you want. This avoids confusion and helps match the style to your hair type. Confirm the Length and Fade Clearly explain the length you want on top and sides. Ask for short, medium, or long length and mention fade type like low or mid fade. This helps your barber create a balanced, clean straight haircut. How to Style Straight Hair for Men Follow these simple steps to style straight hair easily. Each step helps add volume, shape, and clean control. Wash and Prep Your Hair Start by washing your hair with Clarifying Shampoo to remove oil and buildup. Follow with a hydrating conditioner, then towel-dry until damp. Clean, prepped hair styles better and keeps straight hair smooth and manageable. Add Volume at the Roots Straight hair often looks flat, so add lift at the roots. Apply a small amount of Sea Salt Spray to damp hair and gently lift with your fingers. This adds volume, texture, and makes straight hair look fuller. Blow-Dry for Shape Use a blow dryer on medium heat to shape your hair. Lift the roots while drying and guide hair into place. Blow-drying helps set volume, control direction, and makes straight hairstyles last longer. Finish with a Styling Product Finish with a small amount of Texture Clay or Styling Cream. Rub it between your hands and apply lightly for control and definition. These products keep straight hair neat, flexible, and natural without stiffness. How to Maintain Straight Haircuts Maintaining straight haircuts is easy when you follow these simple care and grooming steps. Get Regular Trims Get a trim every 4-6 weeks to keep straight haircuts sharp and tidy. Regular trims remove split ends, keep the shape clean, and stop straight hair from looking flat or messy as it grows out. Keep Hair Healthy Healthy hair makes straight hairstyles look better. Wash hair 2-3 times a week, use a hydrating conditioner, and avoid rough towel drying. A small amount of Forte Series Hydrating Argan Oil helps keep hair smooth, soft, and easy to manage. Avoid Heavy Products Heavy products can weigh straight hair down and make it look greasy. Use lightweight options like Forte Series Styling Cream or Texture Clay to add control and shape without killing volume or natural movement. Best Hair Products for Straight Hair Using the right hair products makes straight hairstyles easier to style, helping add lift, shape, and control without making hair feel heavy. Texture Clay Texture clay helps straight hair hold its shape while adding light texture. It gives a natural, matte finish and prevents hair from looking flat or overly smooth. Molding Paste Molding paste offers flexible hold for straight hair. It helps shape hairstyles, adds control, and allows easy restyling without stiffness or heavy buildup. Pomade Pomade smooths straight hair and adds controlled shine. It works well for side parts and sleek styles, keeping hair neat and polished all day. Styling Cream Styling cream adds soft control and natural movement to straight hair. It reduces flyaways, improves shape, and keeps hair looking healthy without weighing it down. Sea Salt Spray Sea salt spray adds light texture and volume to straight hair. It creates a relaxed, natural finish and helps hair look fuller with easy movement. Texture Powder Texture powder lifts straight hair at the roots and adds instant volume. It creates grip and separation, making thin or flat hair look thicker. Clarifying Shampoo Clarifying shampoo removes product buildup from straight hair. It keeps the scalp clean, boosts natural volume, and helps styling products work better. Hydrating Conditioner Hydrating conditioner softens straight hair and prevents dryness. It improves manageability, adds smoothness, and keeps hair healthy without flattening volume. Hydrating Argan Oil Hydrating argan oil nourishes straight hair and adds shine. It reduces dryness and frizz while keeping hair smooth, light, and easy to manage. FAQs About Straight Hair for Men Which haircut is best for men with straight hair? Textured crops, side parts, and layered cuts work best for straight hair. These styles add shape and movement, helping straight hair look fuller and easier to style daily. Do layers suit straight hair? Yes, layers suit straight hair very well. They reduce flatness, add movement, and create a natural shape, making straight hair look more styled and less stiff. Are there low-maintenance haircuts for straight hair? Yes, short crops, buzz cuts, and simple taper fades are low-maintenance for straight hair. They require minimal styling and stay neat with regular trims. Can men with straight hair get a fade or undercut? Men with straight hair can easily get a fade or undercut. These cuts create clean contrast, highlight sharp lines, and make straight hair look modern and well-defined. Which fade is good for straight hair? Low fades and mid fades work best for straight hair. They blend smoothly, keep the sides clean, and allow the top to stay structured and easy to style. How do I style straight hair for men? Start with clean, dry hair. Apply a small amount of styling cream, comb or finger-style into shape, and focus on adding light texture or volume for a natural finish. How can men add texture to straight hair? Men can add texture to straight hair by using layered cuts, blow-drying with lift, and applying light styling products that create separation and natural movement. How can I add volume to straight hair? Add volume by blow-drying the roots upward, choosing layered haircuts, and avoiding heavy products that flatten straight hair and reduce lift. What products work best for styling straight hair? Lightweight creams, texture clay, sea salt spray, and texture powder work best. These products add control, shape, and movement without making straight hair greasy. How often should I trim straight hair to maintain my haircut? Trim straight hair every 4 to 6 weeks. Regular trims keep the shape sharp, prevent split ends, and help the haircut stay clean and well-balanced.
